prompt: Why is the third generation of video game consoles widely considered to have ended in 2003, despite there not really being any more games made for those consoles in that year?
judge_reasoning: Candidate [3] most directly addresses the prompt’s core issue by explaining that “generation end” dates can reflect broader industry transitions or relevance/support rather than the presence of new games in that specific year, and it does so with relatively low risk of fabricated details. Candidate [2] provides a detailed 2003-specific rationale but relies on many specific claims (laws/regulations, patent-driven cloning dynamics, support closures) that are not well-supported and therefore reduce factual reliability. Candidate [4] includes clearly dubious, highly specific factual assertions (e.g., a Master System “Alex Kidd’s World Adventure” early-2003 Germany claim) that strongly undermine correctness. Candidate [1] mostly reframes/contradicts the premise instead of explaining why 2003 is treated as the endpoint despite few/no games that year.
